script_nghe: Right, next month’s debate. The motion is banning private cars in city centres. It’ll be held on the eighteenth of March — the twenty-fifth was double-booked. Three speakers on each side, seven minutes each, followed by questions. Professor Nakamura has agreed to chair. If you want to speak, register by the tenth.

phan.noi_dung:
**DEBATE SOCIETY — MEETING NOTES**

- Motion to be debated: banning **1** ____________ in city centres
- Date of debate: **2** ____________ March
- Speakers per side: **3** ____________
- Speaking time each: **4** ____________ minutes
- Chair: Professor **5** ____________
- Deadline to register: **6** ____________

> **The congestion charge that worked**
> 
> When London introduced a charge for driving into the city centre in 2003, the scheme was widely predicted to fail. Similar proposals had been rejected in several cities, and public opinion beforehand was hostile. What changed the outcome was not the charge itself but the conditions attached to it: revenue was committed by law to public transport, and several hundred additional buses were introduced before the charge began, not after.
> 
> Traffic entering the zone fell by about 30% within a year and has never returned to previous levels. Journey times improved, and bus reliability rose sharply. Public support, which stood at around 40% before introduction, rose above 50% within two years — a pattern repeated in Stockholm, where a trial scheme was approved in a referendum only after residents had experienced it.
> 
> Not all results were positive. The economic effects on retailers in the zone remain disputed, with studies reaching opposite conclusions depending on which comparison areas were chosen. The charge also proved regressive in the sense that it took a larger share of income from lower earners who still needed to drive, though this group turned out to be smaller than campaigners had assumed.
> 
> Only when the scheme had been running for several years did other cities begin to copy it. Even now, the political obstacle remains what it was in 2003: the benefits arrive gradually and are shared widely, while the costs are immediate and fall on an identifiable group.

**True / False / Not Given (7–10):**
7. Buses were increased before the charge was introduced.
8. Public support for the London scheme fell after two years.
9. Studies agree about the economic effect on retailers in the zone.
10. In Stockholm, residents voted after experiencing the scheme.

**Hoàn thành câu (11–14):**
11. Traffic entering the zone fell by around ____________ within a year.
12. Revenue was committed by law to ____________.
13. The charge was regressive because it took a larger share of income from ____________.
14. Costs are immediate and fall on an ____________ group.

**Bài A (3 điểm):** viết lại 3 câu sau dùng cấu trúc trong ngoặc.

1. The conditions attached to the charge changed the outcome. *(It is/was … that)*
1. Cities need reliable public transport before restricting cars. *(What … is)*
1. The scheme reduced traffic and improved bus reliability. *(Not only … but also — đảo ngữ)*

**Bài B — Task 2 body paragraph (4 điểm):** viết **1 đoạn thân bài 6–7 câu** cho đề *Should city centres be closed to private cars?*
*Tiêu chí: có 1 câu chẻ HOẶC 1 đảo ngữ dùng đúng (2đ) · có 1 câu ngắn dưới 10 từ để tạo nhịp (1đ) · câu chủ đề nêu rõ ý cả đoạn (1đ).*

**P3:** Should driving in city centres be restricted? · Why do people resist paying for things that were free? · How can governments make unpopular policies acceptable?

writing.de_tom_tat: Bài A — viết lại 3 câu dùng cấu trúc nhấn mạnh trong ngoặc.
writing.bai_mau:
CÂU 1 — The conditions attached to the charge changed the outcome. (It is… that)
  → It was the conditions attached to the charge that changed the outcome.
     [nhấn vào chủ ngữ; chú ý dùng was vì hành động ở quá khứ]

CÂU 2 — We need a realistic timetable more than anything else. (What… is)
  → What we need more than anything else is a realistic timetable.
     [mệnh đề What làm chủ ngữ, động từ chính là is]

CÂU 3 — The government has never faced such strong opposition. (Never… đảo ngữ)
  → Never has the government faced such strong opposition.
     [đảo trợ động từ has lên trước chủ ngữ]

BA CÂU BỔ SUNG để luyện thêm:
  · Only after the deadline did they respond.  [Only + trạng ngữ → đảo ngữ]
  · Not only did costs fall, but quality also improved.  [Not only → đảo ngữ]
  · So significant was the change that nobody expected it.  [So + tính từ → đảo ngữ]

cham_diem.tieu_chi: Dùng đúng cấu trúc yêu cầu (2đ)
cham_diem.vi_sao: Câu 1 dùng It was… that đúng thì quá khứ. Câu 2 dùng What… is với động từ số ít. Câu 3 đảo trợ động từ has lên trước chủ ngữ — đúng luật đảo ngữ.
Cả ba câu giữ đúng nghĩa gốc. Cấu trúc nhấn mạnh chỉ đổi trọng tâm, không đổi nội dung.

dang_hoc:
Ba cấu trúc nhấn mạnh chính:
1. It is/was… that… — nhấn vào một thành phần cụ thể
2. What… is/was… — nhấn vào toàn bộ ý
3. Đảo ngữ — nhấn bằng cách phá trật tự thông thường
Luật đảo ngữ: sau Never · Rarely · Seldom · Little · Not only · Only + trạng ngữ · So + tính từ thì đảo trợ động từ lên trước chủ ngữ.
Nếu câu không có trợ động từ thì thêm do/does/did: "Only then did I understand".
Dùng một hoặc hai lần mỗi bài. Nhiều hơn là nghe cố ý và mất tự nhiên.
loi_thuong_gap: ❌ Never the government has faced… → ✅ Never has the government faced… (phải đảo)
❌ What we need are a timetable → ✅ What we need is a timetable (mệnh đề What luôn số ít)
❌ It was the conditions that changed the outcome → nếu gốc là hiện tại thì phải dùng It is
❌ Dùng đảo ngữ 5–6 lần trong một bài → nghe như đang biểu diễn, mất điểm tự nhiên.

speaking.de_tom_tat: Part 3 — dùng cấu trúc nhấn mạnh khi nói để làm quan điểm rõ hơn.

cau_tra_loi.hoi: What is the biggest challenge facing your generation?
cau_tra_loi.mau: What worries me most is housing, honestly. It's not that salaries haven't risen — they have — it's that property prices have risen far faster. Never has the gap between the two been so wide.
cau_tra_loi.ghi_chu: Ba cấu trúc nhấn mạnh trong một câu trả lời: What… is · It's not that… it's that… · Never has…

cau_tra_loi.hoi: Do you think hard work guarantees success?
cau_tra_loi.mau: Not on its own, no. What matters just as much is opportunity — and that isn't distributed equally. Only when both come together do people really get ahead.
cau_tra_loi.ghi_chu: "Only when… do people…" — đảo ngữ trong lời nói, hoàn toàn tự nhiên nếu dùng đúng chỗ.

cau_tra_loi.mau: In most ways, yes. It is the pace of change that people struggle with, rather than the technology itself. Rarely does regulation keep up.
cau_tra_loi.ghi_chu: "It is X that…" và "Rarely does…" — hai cấu trúc nhấn mạnh, mỗi cái một lần.

cham_diem.vi_sao: Cấu trúc nhấn mạnh dùng tự nhiên, không làm ngắt mạch nói.
distributed equally · get ahead · pace of change · keep up.
What worries me most is… · It's not that… it's that… · Never has… · Only when… do… · Rarely does…
Trọng âm câu rơi vào phần được nhấn — đó là cách nhấn mạnh bằng giọng.

meo_noi: Cấu trúc nhấn mạnh trong nói ăn điểm Grammatical Range rất nhanh, nhưng chỉ dùng 1–2 lần mỗi câu trả lời.
"It's not that X — it's that Y" là mẫu câu hữu dụng nhất trong nhóm này. Học thuộc và dùng thường xuyên.
Khi dùng đảo ngữ, nhấn giọng vào phần đầu câu (Never, Only, Rarely) — nếu không nó mất tác dụng.
